neighbours.label: 'last' or 'final' marking the final instance or closing stretch of something ('one last time', 'the final weeks of'), as against first/opening/early
fire: Before the movers came, she walked through the empty house one last time.
The old captain gazed at the harbor one last time before he retired.
During the final months of his life, the painter rarely left his studio.
Supplies ran short in the final days of the siege.
He gave the engine one last try, and it finally started.
The band played one last song for the crowd before the lights went out.
Prices rose sharply in the final years of the old regime.
Many soldiers deserted in the final weeks of the campaign.
quiet: Before the movers came, she walked through the empty house for the first time.
The old captain gazed at the harbor every morning before work.
During the early months of his career, the painter rarely left his studio.
Supplies ran short in the opening days of the siege.
He gave the engine a quick check, and it started.
The band played a slow song for the crowd as the lights dimmed.
Prices rose sharply in the early years of the new regime.
Many soldiers enlisted in the first weeks of the campaign.
